key_insight: Dementia-Agents uses a multi-agent pipeline to turn heterogeneous clinical records into syndrome-level dementia staging and phenotyping decisions rather than focusing only on Alzheimer’s disease.
clinical_relevance: The framework is designed for real-world cognitive neurology settings where missing, mixed, and multi-informant data are common, aiming to improve diagnostic consistency and interpretability.
method: Data agent converts structured records into faithful text while preserving missing-data signals.
Five fine-tuned domain experts generate separate predictions for staging and phenotyping.
Coordinator agent combines expert outputs probabilistically into final decisions.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on 1,066 patients from two cognitive neurology services, the system outperformed monolithic MLLMs and prior medical multi-agent systems in the abstract.
watch_item: Performance gains may depend on local data quality, service-specific workflows, and careful validation before deployment across different clinical settings.
paper_title: Dementia-Agents: A Multi-Modal Multi-Agent System for Dementia Staging and Phenotyping
